status: Provisional, chosen by the map's owner on 2026-11-01 from layer 2d's best guess; may change if the owner decides otherwise. Edit this file and re-run scripts/add_language_layers.py to move it.

hearths.name: West coast
hearths.why: layer 2d: the most productive place on a large landmass, inside the latitude band of Earth's homelands (6 S - 37 N); the model's surroundings picture links the map by land only to the cold north-west, so an on-map hearth is the likelier story (about 70-90 %).

spread.why: layer 2 (Pinhasi, Fort & Ammerman 2005 sites): plain distance from the origin, 1.0 km a year; sea crossings as easy as flat land (every fit chose kappa = 1).

branches.why: illustrative, not tested: a family's branches are the groups that left the spreading front at a given time, the front cut into arcs of about 600 km (primary branches from the front at 700 years, sub-branches from the front at 1,600 years).
